# cb:b583

> /end runs alone, in its own turn, after the session's substantive close is complete; it is never invoked inline in a turn that also does close work. The Stop hook's render only reaches the previous completed turn, so /end run in a later turn reads a render that already includes the close turn and the finalized thread document's embedded transcript body contains it; the only omitted turn is the /end invocation turn itself, which carries no decision content and needs no disclosure. /end invoked inline emits a warning that the current turn will not be captured in the finalized body. Same-turn successive finalization (a /final running the close and the finalize in one turn) does not satisfy this and is rejected: a turn boundary is a separate exchange, not a second skill call.

**Type:** prescription · **Kind:** convention · **Domain:** system · **Status:** active
**Tags:** `threads`, `thread-persistence`, `end-skill`, `observability`, `lifecycle:recurring`
